requirements.title: The web application shall render its interface on a dark, obsidian-toned canvas using the PeakFlames Design System's brand type ramp

vision.paraphrase: Summit adopts the PeakFlames Design System as its visual language, establishing a dark obsidian canvas with Archivo typeface for headings and IBM Plex Sans for body text to create a cohesive, considered product identity.

conops.paraphrase: When the new habit appears in the list after creation, users see it rendered in the dark obsidian canvas with brand typography, establishing visual confidence in the app as a finished product.

requirements.title: The web application shall render exactly one flame-accented "hot" element per view, reserved for the primary action

vision.paraphrase: The PeakFlames Design System's 'one hot element per view' rule ensures only the primary action carries the flame accent, maintaining visual calm and preventing aggressive, distracting UI patterns even with a dark, high-contrast palette.

conops.paraphrase: When the user clicks the Add button to submit a new habit, that button is the single flame-accented primary action on the view, guiding the user's interaction.
When the user clicks the done-today control on a habit card, that control becomes the primary action with flame-accent treatment, emphasizing the moment of daily completion.

requirements.title: The web application shall display a visible focus ring on any interactive control when it receives keyboard focus

vision.paraphrase: Clear visual signaling of interactive elements ensures users can always tell what is interactive at a glance; keyboard focus rings extend this clarity to keyboard-only navigation, supporting full accessibility.

conops.paraphrase: When a user tabs into the habit name input field, a visible focus ring indicates the control is ready for keyboard input, removing ambiguity about where focus currently is.
When a user tabs through habit controls to mark one done, the focused control displays a visible ring, allowing keyboard navigation without requiring a mouse or touch.
When a user tabs to the Active/Archived filter controls, each receives a visible focus ring when focused, enabling keyboard-driven filter switching.

requirements.title: The web application shall indicate the currently selected Active/Archived filter using the PeakFlames Design System's ember gradient treatment

vision.paraphrase: The design system's ember gradient provides a consistent, branded visual indicator for selected state, ensuring users can instantly see which view they are currently in without confusion.

conops.paraphrase: When a user clicks the Archived filter control, the ember gradient treatment visually marks that control as selected, clearly indicating the view has switched from Active to Archived habits.
While viewing archived habits, the Archived filter button displays the ember gradient selection treatment, making it visually obvious which filter is currently active.
